claims.text: Increasing the concentration of magnetic elements in a magnetic high-entropy alloy enhances its magnetic anisotropy.
Enhanced magnetic anisotropy increases the coercive field.
Increasing magnetic-element concentration will produce a higher coercive field than an alloy without that intervention.
The predicted coercivity increase should hold at room temperature and with no external magnetic field.
The proposed relationship is applicable broadly to magnetic high-entropy alloys with varying compositions.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify no external magnetic field, whereas measuring coercive field ordinarily requires sweeping an applied magnetic field; the distinction between effect conditions and measurement conditions is not stated.
